threats.name: Direct IT/OT Communication
threats.description: Controllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.
categories: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0883 Internet Accessible Device
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0886 Remote Services
NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise an IT asset might reach the industrial control system and change, stop or damage the physical process it controls.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary
threats.description: Assets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to disturb the availability of important parts of the system.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Human Use of Machine Identity
threats.description: People who call a service with the account of a machine, like an administrator using the credentials of a service account or a client that ships with an API key of its own, act without an identity of theirs. The service cannot tell them apart, nor require a second factor or end their access when they leave, and the secret gets copied to wherever they work.
categories: OWASP NHI10:2025 Human Use of NHI
OWASP ASI03:2026 Identity and Privilege Abuse

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might use a secret copied from a laptop, a script or a client to access the target, and nobody can tell who did what with it.

threats.name: Insecure Control Protocol
threats.description: Most industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.
categories: IEC 62443-3-3 SR 1.2 Software Process and Device Identification and Authentication
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0855 Unauthorized Command Message
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0830 Adversary-in-the-Middle
NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers in the network might send commands that change, stop or damage the physical process, or alter the commands and readings exchanged with the controller.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Long-Lived Credentials
threats.description: Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who find a leaked secret might use it for a long time to access the target with the permissions of the caller.

threats.name: Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
threats.description: Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify highly sensitive data without strong authentication.

threats.name: Missing Hardening
threats.description: Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier attack high-value targets.

threats.name: Missing Identity Store
threats.description: The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to exploit risks unseen in this threat model in the identity provider/store that is currently missing in the model.

threats.name: Missing Safety System Independence
threats.description: A safety instrumented system brings the process into a safe state when the basic process control fails or is attacked. It only does so when it is independent of that control: when assets other than a dedicated safety engineering workstation can change its program, setpoints or outputs, one compromise can disable the control and the safety function together, as the TRITON attack did.
categories: IEC 61511 Independence of the Safety Instrumented System
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0880 Loss of Safety
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS T0843 Program Download
NIST SP 800-82r3 Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might disable or trip the safety function and so cause explosions, releases of hazardous material or injuries.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Missing Vault (Secret Storage)
threats.description: In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier steal config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.) once a vulnerability to access files is present and exploited.

threats.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
threats.description: When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.
categories: OWASP API7:2023 Server Side Request Forgery

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access sensitive services or files of network-reachable components by modifying outgoing calls of affected components.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V12 - File and Resources Verification Requirements

threats.name: SQL/NoSQL-Injection
threats.description: When a database is accessed via database access protocols SQL/NoSQL-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to modify SQL/NoSQL queries to steal and modify data and eventually further escalate towards a deeper system penetration via code executions.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V5 - Validation, Sanitization and Encoding Verification Requirements

threats.name: Unencrypted Communication
threats.description: Due to the confidentiality and/or integrity rating of the data assets transferred over the communication link this connection must be encrypted.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, network attackers might be able to eavesdrop on unencrypted sensitive data sent between components.

threats.name: Unguarded Access From Internet
threats.description: Internet-exposed assets must be guarded by a protecting service, application, or reverse-proxy.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to directly attack sensitive systems without any hardening components in-between due to them being directly exposed on the internet.

mitigations.name: Industrial DMZ
mitigations.description: Separate IT and OT with an industrial DMZ, so that no communication link crosses from IT into a control zone directly: replicate the historian into the DMZ for IT users, give remote and vendor access only through a jump host there, and filter what passes with firewalls on both sides. Tag the assets in the DMZ with industrial-dmz.

attributes.threagile:check: Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

mitigations.name: Anti-DoS Measures
mitigations.description: Apply anti-DoS techniques like throttling and/or per-client load blocking with quotas. Also for maintenance access routes consider applying a VPN instead of public reachable interfaces. Generally applying redundancy on the targeted technical asset reduces the risk of DoS.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Personal Identities for People
mitigations.description: Let people sign in with their own identity, through single sign-on with multi-factor authentication, and pass it on to the target, modelling the link with the identity end-user. Where an administrator needs the permissions of a service, grant them for a limited time through a privileged access workflow that records who used them. Keep secrets of service accounts out of clients.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Authenticated Control Protocols
mitigations.description: Use the secure variant of the protocol where the devices support it (Modbus/TCP Security, DNP3 over TLS or with Secure Authentication, CIP Security, OPC UA with SignAndEncrypt, S7comm-plus with access protection), and enable the access protection of the controllers. Where the protocol cannot be secured, allow only the expected senders and function codes with an industrial firewall in front of the controller, and keep controllers in RUN mode with the key switch.

attributes.threagile:check: Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

mitigations.name: Short-Lived Credentials
mitigations.description: Replace static secrets between services with a workload identity issued by the platform (cloud IAM roles, Kubernetes service account tokens, SPIFFE), or with short-lived tokens obtained through OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange, and model the link with the identity workload or the authentication short-lived-token. Where a long-lived secret remains, keep it in a vault, scope it narrowly, rotate it automatically and detect its use from unexpected places.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
mitigations.description: Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: System Hardening
mitigations.description: Try to apply all hardening best practices (like CIS benchmarks, OWASP recommendations, vendor recommendations, DevSec Hardening Framework, DBSAT for Oracle databases, and others).

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Identity Store
mitigations.description: Include an identity store in the model if the application has a login.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Safety System Independence
mitigations.description: Let only a dedicated safety engineering workstation, which programs no other controllers, change the safety controller, and give the basic process control and the HMIs readonly access to its status. Keep the key switch of the safety controller in RUN mode outside of maintenance, and alert on every program change.

attributes.threagile:check: Are the recommendations of NIST SP 800-82 and the referenced IEC 62443 requirements applied?

mitigations.name: Vault (Secret Storage)
mitigations.description: Consider using a Vault (Secret Storage) to securely store and access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.).

attributes.threagile:check: GetAttribute a Vault (Secret Storage) in place?

mitigations.name: SSRF Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: SQL/NoSQL-Injection Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to use parameter binding to be safe from injection vulnerabilities. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Encryption of Communication Links
mitigations.description: Apply transport layer encryption to the communication link.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Encapsulation of Technical Asset
mitigations.description: Encapsulate the asset behind a guarding service, application, or reverse-proxy. For admin maintenance a bastion-host should be used as a jump-server. For file transfer a store-and-forward-host should be used as an indirect file exchange platform.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?
